correctness.rationale: In a nonvertical slicing plane, projection sends each azimuthal meridian fiber to an interval along the corresponding radial ray. Its upper and lower plane-support levels increase with cos(azimuth) since R>a; away from the null transition set, annularity is exactly feasibility with nonempty interior at every azimuth, i.e. m<H−R sin θ. Haar cos θ and folded Lebesgue offset give the Jacobian b³xW_R/R², and the common hit conditioning cancels in the conditional density. The supports stay in a fixed bounded x-range. The vertical exposed face gives H′(0+)=q by taking limits of supporting maximizers, so uniformly G_R=1+qx/R+o(R⁻¹), W_R=1+O(R⁻²), and J_R=1/6+q/(3R)+o(R⁻¹); the sliver near x=1 has width and height O(R⁻¹). For q>0 the old triangle is contained in the enlarged support and the normalized density is strictly smaller throughout it, so TV equals the new mass outside, with leading term 6q∫₀¹x²dx/R=2q/R. For q=0 the support symmetric difference and density error are both o(R⁻¹); a C² support gives O(R⁻²). The hit mass is πR/4+O(1) and the annulus mass b³J_R/R². For the unit circle, independent expansion of the fixed-support normalizer gives 1/6+1/(40R²), and integrating the absolute centered second-order density at the sign change x=√(3/10) gives 27/400−9√30/2500. Inspected RESULT.md lines 41–126, VERIFICATION.md and check_marks.py. The 109 recorded checks, including numerical rectangle and ellipse cases, were not rerun; they do not certify arbitrary meridians. The bounds are for each fixed meridian.
